quotes.text: PubMed case reports were selected as the primary source

rationale: The paper names source datasets and platforms, including PubMed case reports, MedQA, and physician-college materials. It does not report a version or snapshot date plus a route from an individual task to its source record.

quotes.text: released under a credentialed-access data use agreement

rationale: S1 reports data origin and collection, and also states access terms and IRB/consent status in the hospital-record passage. This satisfies origin, collection method, terms, and governance.

quotes.text: against the U.S. adult inpatient population

rationale: The paper reports a representativeness comparison of age, sex, and race against a named target population. It also reports the magnitude of differences.
searched: S1-S5. The only explicit safety and bias test-suite statement is in S4 code comments, which do not count as reporting under G1a for this item.

quotes.text: A private held-out test split with concealed labels is excluded from all public surfaces.

rationale: S1 reports developer-side controls including a private held-out split and canary string. It also reports empirical contamination checks using sentence completion and similarity measures.

quotes.text: stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

rationale: The paper explicitly states that agents cannot reach ground-truth answers at runtime. It names mechanisms: separate evaluation service, no network path, and labels not published.

searched: S1-S5. The packet does not report data, software, simulator, and judge pinning at release. The paper also describes live LLM-based mapper/parser components rather than a fully frozen external-free harness.

quotes.text: all 120 reference solutions were graded correct

rationale: S1 states that scripted reference solutions were run through the grader. It reports that all reference solutions were graded correct.

quotes.text: all other records remain unchanged

rationale: S1 reports that the grader checks intended state changes and unchanged records. This directly satisfies detection of out-of-scope modifications.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks

rationale: The appendix reports an empirical random-action success rate. It also states that chance success rates are reported per metric.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks

rationale: S1 reports a random-action agent result across tasks. The anchor allows a do-nothing or random agent score reported for all tasks.

quotes.text: finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%

rationale: The benchmark reports validation of its own grader on injected outcomes. It gives error figures for false accepts and false rejects.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed

rationale: S1 reports temperature 0 and a fixed seed. It also states a repeated-run policy of three runs per task.

quotes.text: test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test

rationale: The paper reports confidence intervals and a paired permutation test for a model comparison. This satisfies the headline comparison criterion.

quotes.text: each task is run three times

rationale: S1 reports three runs per task and a seed/temperature policy. It does not state whether runs are independent.

quotes.text: where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead

rationale: S1 reports 95% confidence intervals, the resampling unit, and an adjustment for clustering when tasks share patients. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: agreement rates of the final environment state across these eight runs

rationale: S1 reports eight repeated executions with final environment-state agreement and pass^8. It does not report action-sequence agreement.

quotes.text: Qwen3-235b-a22b, April 2025

rationale: S1 gives model names with release dates for at least some evaluated models and reports temperature settings. It does not state a harness version, tag, or commit matching the reported results.

quotes.text: Tools are specified using JSON schemas with name, arguments, and types.

rationale: S1 reports JSON schemas, side-effect documentation, and return/error semantics. It also says agent prompts include these tool descriptions, so side-effect disclosure reaches the agent-visible surface.

quotes.text: Two tools are simulated stubs that return fixed placeholder responses

rationale: S1 reports conformance tests and discloses simulated stub tools. It also states that the simulated-stub disclosure appears in tool descriptions shown to the agent.

quotes.text: Two tools are simulated stubs that return fixed placeholder responses

rationale: The benchmark includes clinical orders or investigation actions, so the item applies. S1 discloses simulated tool behavior reaching tool descriptions, but it does not clearly identify which actions mutate or are irreversible, or whether unsafe/unnecessary writes are scored.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.

rationale: S1 names the grader input as the final environment state. Because this is an end-state grader, no non-state rationale is required, and S1 reports validation on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with error rates.

quotes.text: Web access is blocked during runs

rationale: S1 reports controls on leakage through web/retrieval, a private held-out split with concealed labels, and a canary string on released tasks. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: Subgroup analysis demonstrated variation in model performance across different specialty groups

rationale: S1 reports results by specialty/task-family slices and reports slice sizes for specialties elsewhere. Demographic fields exist, but no performance results by patient demographic subgroup are reported.

quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database

rationale: S1 states that patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database. It reports governance through IRB waiver and credentialed-access DUA, and terms separate from the code license.
